findings.finding: The quarter and the full-year guide are already public: on 2026-10-16 14:30 Tokyo Steel revised H1 op to -3.5bn (from -4.0bn) and FY op to +1.0bn (from -4.0bn), ordinary to +2.0bn (from -2.5bn), net to +7.0bn (from +1.0bn, helped by asset sales); the stock rose from 1,643 to 1,706 over two sessions, so the main item a Japanese print turns on is pre-released and a second revision a week later is unlikely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance changes drive this name: 2024-10-25 FY cut -10.5% to next close; 2025-07-18 cut -7.0%; 2025-10-17 cut -6.6%; 2026-01-23 cut -5.9%; 2026-10-16 raise +3.8% (Yahoo daily bars, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/5423.T?range=3y&interval=1d). This time the change landed a week early.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: that is the point of this finding. It removes the guidance line from the print; residual risk is only the H2 ramp (H1 op -3.5bn to FY +1.0bn implies H2 op +4.5bn) being questioned in the 決算説明 material, against a company that cut its guide three times in FY2026.
findings.independence: kabutan/MINKABU coverage of the same disclosure, https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=5423&b=n202610160765 (same document, counts once).

findings.finding: Buyback capacity is exhausted and a new authorisation is plausible at this print: the April 2026 programme (cap 1.5m shares / 2.7bn yen) was completed early on 2026-09-18 at 1.5m shares / 2.59bn yen, an activist (Oasis, ~8.7%, voted against the president in June) is on the register, PBR is 0.77, and FY net was just raised to 7.0bn; against that, the stated policy (total return ratio 25-30%) is already exceeded by the 40-yen dividend alone (~4bn), and Tokyo Steel has not announced a buyback at either of its last two H1 prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2024-07-26 Q1 print with a 10bn-yen / 6.26% buyback: +21.3% to next close; 2026-04-24 FY print with a 2.7bn / 1.46% buyback alongside a dividend cut and a loss guide: -2.3%. H1 prints 2024-10-25 and 2025-10-17 carried no buyback (kabutan disclosure lists).
findings.why_not_priced: Whether the board re-authorises is not knowable before the release; the price carries no visible anticipation (stock down 3.3% this morning, 5d -2.2%), whereas a priced buyback would show as a run-in after the 10-16 revision. Sized as ~25% chance of a 2-3% authorisation worth +3-4%, net of a small disappointment if none.
findings.independence: Policy and dividend: FY短信 2026-04-24 https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260424/140120260424510082.pdf ; Oasis campaign: https://www.zaikei.co.jp/releases/3438036/ (both different documents; the policy cuts against, the activist points for).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-19 Tokyo Steel raised November contract prices by 3,000 yen/t on all products, citing cost-push and data-centre/semiconductor-plant steel demand, while its domestic scrap purchase prices had been cut through August (H2 grade 47,000-50,000 yen/t on 2026-08-21), so the metal spread behind the H2 ramp is widening after the guide was set.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Monthly price announcements move the stock modestly: 2026-10-20 close +0.3% after the November hike (Yahoo bars). The guide-raise of 10-16 on the same spread logic bought +3.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike itself is public and largely priced; what is not is whether management's H2 assumptions in the 決算説明 already include it. The 10-16 notice says implemented price revisions 'will be reflected progressively', which suggests the November step may be partly upside to the guide. Small, because it lands inside a guide the company just set.

outside_window.finding: December contract prices are normally announced around the 20th of the prior month; a further hike or hold would land ~2026-11-20, after the window.
